tasks.title: Hi from the UART
tasks.statement: The soft processor prints text through a UART, a device at address 0x10000000: a byte written (sb) to this address appears in the console. Print “Hi!” and a newline (four bytes in all) and stop with the ebreak instruction. li puts the address in a register, and a character code can be written in quotes: li t1, 'H'.
tasks.hint: The UART address is 0x10000000; let it sit in t0. For each character: li t1, 'H' and sb t1, 0(t0). The newline is the number 10. The last instruction is ebreak.

tasks.title: String up to the zero byte
tasks.statement: The memory (in the task's data) holds the string msg: “Hello, RISC-V!” with a newline and a zero byte at the end. Print it to the UART: walk along the string with a pointer (lbu reads a byte) until you meet the zero. The label msg is available in your code: la t1, msg.
tasks.hint: Keep the string pointer in t1 (la t1, msg). In a loop: lbu t2, 0(t1); if t2 is zero (beqz), it is the end; otherwise sb t2, 0(t0); addi t1, t1, 1; j loop.

tasks.title: LED pattern
tasks.statement: The LEDs are a device at address 0x10001000: the low 8 bits of the written word light LED0…LED7. Light the pattern 1010 0101 (LED7, LED5, LED2 and LED0), that is, write the number 0xA5 (sw), and stop.
tasks.hint: li t0, 0x10001000 is the LED address; li t1, 0xA5 is the pattern; sw t1, 0(t0).

tasks.title: Switches → LEDs
tasks.statement: The switches are a device at address 0x10001004: a read returns their state (8 bits). Read the switches and light the LEDs (0x10001000) with the INVERTED pattern: where a switch is on, the LED is off, and vice versa. The switches are currently set to 1011 0010.
tasks.hint: lw reads the switches; not (that is, xori with −1) flips all 32 bits, but the LEDs need only the low 8: add andi t2, t2, 0xff (or just write it, since the device takes only 8 bits anyway).

tasks.title: Sum from 1 to 100
tasks.statement: Compute the sum of all integers from 1 to 100 with a loop and put the result in register a0, then stop with the ebreak instruction. The expected answer is 5050.
tasks.hint: Two registers: the sum (initially 0) and the counter (initially 1). In a loop: add the counter to the sum, increment the counter, repeat until it exceeds 100 (blt counter, 101, loop; load the limit into a register).

tasks.title: Uppercase letters in memory
tasks.statement: The task's data holds the string text: “risc-v is fun!” (with a zero byte). Make all the Latin letters uppercase right in memory: “RISC-V IS FUN!”. Do not touch the other characters (the hyphen, the spaces, “!”). The difference between an uppercase and a lowercase letter is 32.
tasks.hint: Walk along with a pointer: lbu reads, sb writes. A letter is lowercase if 'a' ≤ code ≤ 'z': skip everything below 'a' (bltu) or above 'z' (bltu with swapped registers). Otherwise subtract 32 and write it back.

tasks.title: Factorial: function and stack
tasks.statement: Write a recursive function fact(n) = n! and call it with n = 6: the result (720) must end up in a0. The calling convention: the argument and the result are in a0; the function must save the return address ra on the stack before calling itself; the stack grows downward (sp decreases). The main program already calls fact, so just write the function. At the end the stack must be back in place.
tasks.hint: The function prologue: addi sp, sp, -16; sw ra, 12(sp); sw s0, 8(sp); mv s0, a0 (we save n in s0, which is a “preserved” register). If n < 2, return 1. Otherwise: a0 = n − 1; call fact; mul a0, a0, s0. The epilogue: lw s0, 8(sp); lw ra, 12(sp); addi sp, sp, 16; ret.

tasks.title: Sorting an array of words
tasks.statement: The task's data has n, the number of elements (8), and arr, an array of signed 32-bit WORDS: 5, −3, 99, 0, −100, 42, 7, −1. Sort the array in place in ascending order. Words take four bytes each, so the address of element i is arr + 4·i (a slli shift by 2). Compare as signed (blt/bge), otherwise the negative numbers would turn out to be the “largest”.
tasks.hint: Bubble sort as in Mini-8, but the step is four bytes: lw t3, 0(t2) and lw t4, 4(t2) read the neighbors, and sw puts them back in the opposite order. Multiply the element index by 4 with slli.

tasks.title: Blinking on a timer
tasks.statement: The timer is a device at address 0x10002000: a read returns the number of instructions executed. Make LED0 blink: eight toggles in a row (on, off, on…), and each state must last at least 200 clock cycles. Make the delay by waiting: remember the time, then read the timer until it has moved forward by 200.
tasks.hint: A loop of eight passes: write 1 or 0 to the LEDs (flip t3 with xori t3, t3, 1); remember the time with lw t4, 0(t1); add 200; in the wait loop read the timer and compare it with the limit (bltu).
